title: High-throughput screening of SIRT7 inhibitors using fluorescent peptide technology
author: Kang, Lu, et al.
materials: includes steps like cell lysis, plasmid binding to the column, washing, and elution. Other Midi plasmid kits (e.g., Thermo Fisher Scientific, Cat#K0481; Geneaid, Cat#PI025; or QIAGEN, Cat#

steps.title: Amplify and isolate SIRT7 plasmid
steps.instruction: Prepare the pET‑28a SIRT7 plasmid and obtain high‑quality midi‑scale DNA for downstream work.

substeps.instruction: Store the pET‑28a plasmid containing human SIRT7 at –20 °C and thaw on ice.
Keep DH5α competent cells at –80 °C; thaw on ice before use.
Add 2 µL of 300 ng/µL plasmid to 100 µL DH5α cells, incubate 30 min on ice.
Heat‑shock at 42 °C for 90 s, then place on ice for 3 min.
Add 300 µL antibiotics‑free LB medium, culture 1 h at 37 °C, 220 rpm shaking.
Spread 50 µL of the transformed suspension onto LB agar containing 50 µg/mL kanamycin; incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C without shaking.
Pick a single colony and inoculate into 100 mL LB + 50 µg/mL kanamycin; grow 12–16 h at 37 °C, 220 rpm.
Extract plasmid DNA with the TIANpure Midi Plasmid Kit, elute with 2 mL ddH₂O.
Measure plasmid concentration on a NanoPhotometer (Nucleic Acid mode): blank with 2 µL ddH₂O, then measure 2 µL sample; record A260/A280.
Store purified plasmid at –20 °C until needed.

steps.title: Transform plasmid into expression host
steps.instruction: Introduce the SIRT7 construct into BL21(DE3) cells for protein production.

substeps.instruction: Store BL21(DE3) competent cells at –80 °C; thaw on ice.
Add 2 µL of 300 ng/µL plasmid to 100 µL BL21(DE3) cells, incubate 30 min on ice.
Heat‑shock at 42 °C for 90 s, then place on ice for 3 min.
Add 300 µL antibiotics‑free LB medium, culture 1 h at 37 °C, 220 rpm shaking.
Spread 50 µL onto LB agar with 50 µg/mL kanamycin; incubate 12–16 h at 37 °C without shaking.

steps.title: Express and lyse SIRT7 protein
steps.instruction: Grow transformed BL21 cells, induce SIRT7 expression, and harvest soluble protein.

substeps.instruction: Inoculate a single transformed colony into 30 mL LB + 50 µg/mL kanamycin in a conical flask.
Incubate at 37 °C, 220 rpm until OD₆₀₀ reaches 0.6–0.8.
Transfer 20–30 mL of this culture into 2 L fresh LB + 50 µg/mL kanamycin (1:50–1:100 scale‑up).
Grow at 37 °C, 220 rpm until OD₆₀₀ again reaches 0.6–0.8.
Add 1 mL IPTG stock to achieve a final concentration of 0.5 mM.
Incubate at 18 °C for 12–16 h, 220 rpm shaking.
Harvest cells by centrifugation at 4 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant and store pellets at –80 °C if not processed immediately.
Resuspend pellets in 150 mL binding buffer containing 1× protease inhibitor cocktail.
Disrupt cells with an ultra‑high‑pressure continuous‑flow disrupter for 10 min at 100 MPa, 4 °C. Optional: sonicate 30 cycles of 5 s ON/5 s OFF at 60 % power if viscosity is high.
Centrifuge lysate at 20 000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C; collect supernatant.
Filter supernatant through a 0.45 µm filter, keep on ice.

steps.title: Purify SIRT7 by HisTrap chromatography
steps.instruction: Capture His‑tagged SIRT7 on a nickel column and elute with an imidazole gradient.

substeps.instruction: Keep all purification steps cold (ice‑water bath, refrigerator, or cold room).
Set up the laboratory pump apparatus and connect a 5 mL HisTrap HP column.
Wash the column with 5 column volumes of ddH₂O.
Equilibrate the column with 5 column volumes of binding buffer (contains 20 mM imidazole).
Load the filtered cell lysate onto the column; waste flows through.
Attach the column to a Unique AutoPure instrument (or ÄKTA system).
Wash with binding buffer until the UV absorbance reaches a steady baseline.
Elute with a linear 0–100 % elution‑buffer gradient over 30 column volumes (flow rate 5 mL/min).
Record UV absorbance and collect fractions in 5 mL tubes at the UV peak.

steps.title: Analyze fractions by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Assess purity of collected fractions using Coomassie‑stained SDS‑PAGE.

substeps.instruction: Mix 16 µL of each fraction with 4 µL 5× loading buffer.
Heat samples at 95 °C for 5 min to denature proteins.
Prepare a 10 % precast gel and place it in the electrophoresis chamber.
Load 4 µL protein ladder into the first well, then 10 µL of each denatured sample into subsequent wells.
Run the stacking gel at 90 V for 30 min, then the separating gel at 120 V for 90 min.
Stain the gel with CBB fast staining solution for 2 h at 20–25 °C.
Rinse the gel with ddH₂O at 50–60 °C for 10 min.
Capture gel images with a chemiluminescent imager.

steps.title: Concentrate and size‑exclude SIRT7
steps.instruction: Concentrate pooled peak fractions and perform SEC for final polishing.

substeps.instruction: Transfer His‑SIRT7 eluates into an Amicon Ultra centrifugal filter.
Centrifuge at 7 000 × g for 30 min at 4 °C until volume is <2 mL.
Load the concentrated protein into a syringe.
Attach the syringe and a Superdex 75 10/300 GL column to the FPLC system.
Equilibrate the SEC column with 1.5 column volumes of SEC buffer.
Inject the sample and run size‑exclusion chromatography.
Collect fractions; analyze a small fraction by SDS‑PAGE as above.
Pool peak fractions eluting between 75 mL and 85 mL.
Concentrate pooled peak fractions with an Amicon filter to a final concentration of 6–10 mg/mL.

steps.title: Measure protein concentration and store
steps.instruction: Determine final SIRT7 concentration and preserve aliquots for future use.

substeps.instruction: Power on the NanoPhotometer and select “Protein UV” mode.
Blank with 2 µL SEC buffer, then measure 2 µL of the concentrated SIRT7 sample; record concentration.
Aliquot the protein into 50 µL portions at ~8.5 mg/mL, snap‑freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at –80 °C.

description: SIRT7 presents great potential as a drug target for the treatment of various diseases. SIRT7 is an NAD+-dependent deacetylase that acts on the acetylated lysine 18 site of histone H3 (H3K18ac) that maintains the fundamental properties of cancer cell phenotypes.2 Additionally, coumarin and its derivatives possess excellent fluorescent properties for labeling biomacromolecules.3 To detect SIRT7 enzymatic activity, we modified the R group of H31-22 peptides at lysine 18 with fluorophore 7-methoxycoumarin-4-acetic acid (MCA). When SIRT7, the peptides and nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) are mixed, SIRT7 protein deacylates peptides to release MCA probe that enhances fluorescent signal. Furthermore, NAD+ hydrolysis product nicotinamide (NAM) effectively inhibits SIRT7 enzymatic activity as the pan-sirtuins inhibitor.4 By using the microplate reader, we developed this luminescent system that enables rapid screening of SIRT7 inhibitors and determination of the IC50 values for tested compounds. Moreover, through the replacement of substrate peptides and corresponding purified enzymes, our protocol could be adapted to identify inhibitors of other epigenetic enzymes.
